ruling.recommended_action: Record the RD-1 breach on driver B-0016's file (unexcused 4.84 km off-route segment, no consent, no traffic cause); keep the $34.38 RydeX fixed fare as charged — the RD-2 refundable amount is zero. No account flag (RD-6 profile condition unmet).

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 09:06–09:13 added 4.84 km (F3). Consent under RD-5 requires a rider message sent before the segment; the complete, timestamped chat (F9) holds only the 08:49 rider pickup note (F7) and the 08:49 driver arrival note (F8), neither naming a road, area or route, and the driver's post-trip statement (F10) is not rider consent (RD-5, G11). No rider-named stop exists (RD-3(a) inapplicable) and no RD-4 traffic cause applies: no incident (F13) and bands 4–5 (F11, F12) are not band 1/2. Segment counts under RD-1/RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's traffic justification fails: no incident was recorded near the route in the trip window (F13) and the only speed records are Ayer Rajah Expressway band 5 and Central Expressway band 4 (F11, F12), neither band 1 or 2, so neither exempts nor corroborates an exemption under RD-4(a)/(b), and RD-4(c) requires the segment to be treated under RD-2.

The claim that no consent exists is accepted, but it does not assist the driver: an unconsented, unexplained deviation (F3) breaches the shortest-and-most-direct-route duty under RD-1; absence of a rider stop request under RD-3(a) leaves the segment counted under RD-2.

The request for no refund is granted, but not because the deviation is excused: the segment counts (F3, RD-1/RD-5) and only the fixed-fare pricing under RD-2 makes the refundable amount zero (F4, F6).
